officialTitle: MONARCH 3: Abemaciclib As Initial Therapy for Advanced Breast Cancer
setting: First-line advanced (no prior systemic therapy in the advanced setting)

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: MONARCH 3 is a double-blind, randomized phase III study of abemaciclib or placebo plus a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor in 493 postmenopausal women with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer who had no prior systemic therapy in the advanced setting.

clinicalQuestion: Does adding abemaciclib to a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor improve PFS as initial therapy for postmenopausal HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer?

pico.population: Postmenopausal women with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, no prior systemic therapy in the advanced setting
pico.intervention: Abemaciclib 150 mg twice daily plus anastrozole or letrozole
pico.outcomes: Primary: investigator-assessed PFS. Secondary: response, safety

arms.label: Abemaciclib + NSAI
arms.regimen: Abemaciclib plus nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor (anastrozole or letrozole)
arms.dosing: Abemaciclib 150 mg twice daily continuous; anastrozole 1 mg or letrozole 2.5 mg daily
arms.doseSourceQuote: Patients received abemaciclib or placebo (150 mg twice daily continuous schedule) plus either 1 mg anastrozole or 2.5 mg letrozole, daily.

arms.label: Placebo + NSAI
arms.regimen: Placebo plus nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor (anastrozole or letrozole)

publications.title: MONARCH 3: Abemaciclib As Initial Therapy for Advanced Breast Cancer.
publications.label: Planned interim analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: Median progression-free survival was significantly prolonged in the abemaciclib arm (hazard ratio, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.41 to 0.72; P = .000021; median: not reached in the abemaciclib arm, 14.7 months in the placebo arm).
In patients with measurable disease, the objective response rate was 59% in the abemaciclib arm and 44% in the placebo arm ( P = .004).

safety.description: Diarrhoea with abemaciclib, any grade (mainly grade 1)
safety.sourceQuote: In the abemaciclib arm, diarrhea was the most frequent adverse effect (81.3%) but was mainly grade 1 (44.6%).
Comparing abemaciclib and placebo, the most frequent grade 3 or 4 adverse events were neutropenia (21.1% v 1.2%), diarrhea (9.5% v 1.2%), and leukopenia (7.6% v 0.6%).

strengths: Continuous-dosing CDK4/6 inhibitor schedule tested in first-line setting
limitations: Primary analysis at a planned interim with immature median PFS in the experimental arm
OS not reported in the primary publication; registry ID not printed in the PubMed abstract

clinicalImplications.text: Supports abemaciclib plus a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor as a first-line option for postmenopausal HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, with a toxicity profile dominated by diarrhoea rather than neutropenia.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Abemaciclib's signature toxicity is diarrhoea (mostly low grade) — counsel patients and pre-arrange antidiarrhoeal management at initiation.
